metadados.title: PELOD Scale - Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction
metadados.description: The PELOD Scale (Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction) is a tool for assessing organ failure in children, mainly used in pediatric intensive care units (PICU).

Based on the assessment of organ dysfunctions in pediatrics.

Processing clinical reasoning...

A NANDA diagnosis requires a careful evaluation of its taxonomies and the search for defining characteristics and related factors. The disclosure of diagnoses on this scale serves only an educational purpose, to promote its use and help users become familiar with the various diagnoses. Under no circumstances should it induce the user to indiscriminately apply any nursing diagnosis without the support of clinical findings obtained through history taking, physical examination, and other systematic tools that will guide the nurse in prescribing care.

Exemplifying with NANDA: NANDA diagnoses related to the identified problems (Educational purpose)
Based on the assessment of organ dysfunctions in pediatrics.

Processing clinical reasoning...

A NANDA diagnosis requires a careful evaluation of its taxonomies and the search for defining characteristics and related factors. The disclosure of diagnoses on this scale serves only an educational purpose, to promote its use and help users become familiar with the various diagnoses. Under no circumstances should it induce the user to indiscriminately apply any nursing diagnosis without the support of clinical findings obtained through history taking, physical examination, and other systematic tools that will guide the nurse in prescribing care.

Scientific Reference
LETEURTRE, S. et al. Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction (PELOD) Score. Pediatric Critical Care Medicine , v. 4, n. 2, p. 177-183, 2003.
LETEURTRE, S. et al. The PELOD-2 score for predicting mortality in pediatric intensive care unit patients. Critical Care Medicine , v. 42, n. 10, p. 2179-2187, 2014.

Score Interpretation

Low Risk (0-5 points)
Reduced mortality risk, mild or absent organ failure.

Moderate Risk (6-10 points)
Intermediate risk. Presence of dysfunctions requiring constant monitoring.

High Risk (11-15 points)
High probability of mortality. Multiple organ failure, requires intensive intervention (PICU).
